item.title: Some people in Tinubu’s administration don’t want Fashola – Ex-presidential aide
item.description: Former presidential aide Laolu Akande has alleged that some individuals close to President Bola Tinubu opposed the appointment of the former Minister of Works and Housing Babatunde Fashola to the current administration. In an interview on the Naija Unfiltered podcast, published by Symfoni TV on Friday, Akande attributed Fashola’s absence from the Federal Government partly to possible fatigue on his part but said resistance from people within the President’s circle was a more significant reason. “I think the reason why Fashola is not in this government, two reasons. I think Fashola himself has a bit of fatigue; more importantly, I think there are people around the president who don’t want to see Fashola because Fashola is not going to tolerate many of those things that you are seeing around,” Akande said. He described the former minister as someone who stands firmly by his principles and would not compromise to accommodate practices he considers unacceptable. “Whatever you say about Fashola, he doesn’t take nonsense and the people who wanted to get some nonsense going, they didn’t want Fashola,” he said. Akande did not disclose the identities of the individuals he accused of opposing Fashola’s inclusion in the administration. He also failed to provide specific examples of the alleged practices they wanted to protect. Fashola was Lagos State governor from 2007 to 2015 before joining the cabinet of former President Muhammadu Buhari. Akande maintained that the former governor remained close to President Tinubu despite his non-inclusion in the administration. “Even somebody like Fashola, who is still very close to the president, no problems openly,” he said. The former presidential aide also questioned whether Tinubu was making sufficient use of capable individuals who could challenge his decisions when necessary. He argued that effective governance required people who could disagree with the President when they believed his decisions or the actions of those around him were wrong. Akande cited Fashola as an example of a politician who would stand his ground, alleging that some individuals within Tinubu’s circle preferred not to have such a figure in the administration. item.title: Tinubu, Shettima flag off APC 2027 campaign in Kaduna
item.description: President Bola Tinubu arrived in Kaduna State on Saturday ahead of the flag-off of the All Progressives Congress’ 2027 presidential campaign, with Vice President Kashim Shettima and his wife, Nana, also arriving for the event. APC National Chairman, Prof Nentawe Yilwatda, the Director-General of the presidential campaign, Abdul’aziz Yari, and Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani were at the airport to welcome the President. Shettima’s arrival was announced in a statement by his spokesman, Stanley Nkwocha. Mr Nkwocha said APC governors, party leaders, elected officials, political stakeholders and supporters were gathering at the Kaduna Township Stadium for the commencement of the party’s nationwide presidential campaign. He described the event as a significant moment for Kaduna, noting that the city would serve as the launching point for the APC’s campaign ahead of the 2027 presidential election. According to the statement, the campaign would provide the ruling party with an opportunity to present its “Renewed Hope 2.0” agenda and highlight the achievements of the Tinubu administration. “The stage is set. Kaduna is ready. The 2027 campaign begins!” the statement read in part. It added, “Asiwaju is here. Northwest for the takeaway!” Ahead of the President’s arrival, security operatives on Saturday barricaded strategic locations across Kaduna metropolis as authorities stepped up security preparations for the campaign event. Personnel from the Nigerian Army, Department of State Services, Nigeria Police Force, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Nigeria Immigration Service and the Kaduna State Vigilance Service were deployed to different parts of the city. The security personnel were stationed at major roundabouts and along roads leading to the venue of the campaign flag-off. Muhammadu Buhari Way, formerly known as WAFF Road, was blocked by security operatives ahead of the expected movement of the President and his entourage through the route. The Ahmadu Bello Stadium roundabout was also manned by heavily armed soldiers, police officers and plain-clothes security personnel. The security restrictions affected traffic in several parts of Kaduna, triggering a gridlock that extended from Junction Road to Ahmadu Bello Way. item.title: French Montana, Jorja Smith to perform at Ballon d’Or 2026
item.description: Ballon d’Or organisers revealed on Saturday that star US rapper French Montana and English singer Jorja Smith would perform at this year’s ceremony, part of efforts to draw more viewers to the awards event. Last year saw Canadian singer Charlotte Cardin do her best to lift the somewhat stiff atmosphere at the prize giving in Paris as she performed her hit “Feel Good” in front of a motionless crowd of suited footballers and VIPs at a theatre. The most prestigious individual award in football will be handed out in London next Monday, with Kylian Mbappe, Spanish pair Lamine Yamal and Ferran Torres, PSG duo Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Harry Kane all seen as frontrunners. It is the first time the Ballon d’Or ceremony, now in its 70th edition, will be hosted in Britain. French Montana has over 30 million monthly listeners on Spotify, mixing Moroccan influences, trap, afrobeat and New York hip hop culture. He has collaborated on hits with Drake, Cardi B and Swae Lee, with whom he made the 2017 track “Unforgettable”, which has racked up 1.9 billion views on YouTube. English singer-songwriter Jorja Smith mixes RnB, soul and jazz influences, drawing on her Jamaican heritage and her classical music training. Her career took off 10 years ago with “Blue Lights”, followed by other tracks ranging from intimate to more danceable. In addition to their “exclusive performances” during the evening, “other surprises are planned”, the Groupe L’Equipe, which organises the ceremony, said in a statement sent to AFP. The group owns the magazine France Football, which has been awarding the Ballon d’Or since 1956. It is based on voting by a jury of journalists from the top 100 countries in the FIFA rankings. In 2025, the top male player prize was awarded to France’s Ousmane Dembele and the women’s to Spain’s Aitana Bonmati. The ceremony will be broadcast on sports streaming website DAZN, and the L’Equipe TV channel in France. It will be hosted by former France and Arsenal striker Thierry Henry, and sports journalist Kate Scott. In 2022, tenor Andrea Bocelli was chosen to open the ceremony. item.title: NDC fixes October 26 for 3rd NEC meeting, campaign council unveiling
item.description: …Says 80 per cent of its candidates could not afford the Expression of Interest forms By Henry Umoru The national leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, has fixed Monday, October 26, for its third National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting, where it will unveil its National Campaign Council and present its candidates with Certificates of Return. The party has attributed its limited financial resources partly to the economic hardship in the country, just as it claimed that about 80 per cent of its candidates could not afford the Expression of Interest forms. According to the NDC, it had to issue the forms to the affected candidates free of charge, contrary to what he described as public speculation about its finances. In a statement signed on Saturday by NDC National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, he disclosed that the meeting would also feature the presentation of the party’s statement of account by its National Treasurer. According to him, it is part of the party’s commitment to transparency and accountability in the management of its finances, just as it challenged other political parties, particularly the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), to adopt similar measures in disclosing their financial records, adding, “For the NDC, it is no longer politics as usual.” The statement read, “The leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) wishes to announce that its 3rd National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting will hold on Monday, 26th October, 2026, at JD event centre, Kashim Ibrahim Way, opposite A-class park, Maitama, Abuja. Time is 10 am prompt. “A major highlight of the meeting will be the release and presentation of the party’s Statement of Account by the National Treasurer. This is in deference to our avowed commitment to the principles of transparency and accountability. In this regard, we challenge other political parties, especially the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), to emulate this level of openness and transparency in the management of their finances. “For the NDC, it is no longer politics as usual. “Our finances would have been more robust. However, contrary to speculations in the public domain, and due to the level of poverty, hunger and deprivation in the country occasioned by the rudderless APC and its amorphous economic policies, about 80% of our candidates could not afford the Expression of Interest forms. item.title: Man City beaten by Aston Villa to end perfect Premier League start
item.description: Manchester City’s perfect Premier League start came to a crashing halt in a 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa as Nicolas Jackson’s double extended an upturn in form for Unai Emery’s new-look side. Enzo Maresca had become the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a new club but failed to find a solution to City’s struggles at Villa Park, where they have now lost for the past four seasons. After Jackson blasted home the opener after just six minutes, Villa relied on a brilliant goalkeeping display from Zion Suzuki to keep City at bay. Erling Haaland breifly levelled early in the second half only for Villa to respond on the hour mark when Jackson drilled home Ibrahim Mbaye’s cross. Four years on from Emery’s arrival, which has transformed the club from a sleeping giant into the Champions League, the Spaniard is working more magic despite seeing the spine of his squad in recent seasons decimated. Six of the side that started Villa’s victory in last season’s Europa League left during the transfer window. But the recruitment of the likes of Jackson, Suzuki, Mbaye and Johan Manzambi is already paying dividends after a slow start to the campaign. Until now City have managed to shrug off the cloud hanging over the club’s Premier League future to keep winning on the field. The 10-time English champions are appealing a guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking financial rules between 2009 and 2018 that could lead to swingeing sanctions, including relegation. There was little sign of that distraction affecting Enzo Maresca’s men, but they were made to pay for two sloppy defensive errors. A heavy touch by Marc Guehi presented Jackson with possession for the opening goal as he cut inside Elliott Anderson and blasted high past Gianluigi Donnarumma. City largely dominated the remainder of the first half, but could not find a way past Suzuki. Iliman Ndiaye, Rayan Cherki and Abdukodir Khusanov were all denied before Ndiaye struck the post. City’s pressure finally told on 52 minutes when Haaland powered in a header from Ndiaye’s cross for his 13th goal in 10 appearances this season. Josko Gvardiol nearly completed the comeback when Suzuki turned his blistering drive into the crossbar moments later. Instead, it was Villa to got the decisive third goal. Mbaye was played in behind the City defence and from his cross, Jackson’s low effort should have been saved by Donnarumma. The visitors pressed in vain for another equaliser to allow Arsenal the chance to move level on points at the top of the table when they host Everton later on Saturday. item.title: Thousands March In France Against Far-Right Party Congress
item.description: Thousands of people yelling anti-fascist slogans marched in the French city of Orléans Saturday against a congress by far-right leader Marine Le Pen’s National Rally (RN) party there, AFP journalists saw. The protest — held on a day of fresh nationwide demonstrations over the cost of living after ones a week ago that devolved into street violence — criticised both Le Pen and centrist President Emmanuel Macron. But registered voters are not actual votes, political endorsements are not public opinion, and the North is not a single electoral personality. That is the political signal this week. Why Kaduna matters Kaduna is in the North-West region. Kaduna is an appropriate starting point because it captures both the opportunity and the danger confronting Tinubu. It is a major political centre in the North-West, but it is not naturally secure territory for the President. Tinubu lost Kaduna to Atiku Abubakar in 2023. The state also embodies several issues that could determine northern voting behaviour: insecurity, rural poverty, food prices, religious sensitivity and the relationship between elite political agreements and popular sentiment. By beginning there, the APC is signalling that it will not concede the region to Atiku merely because he is a northern Muslim. It is relying on Vice-President Kashim Shettima, governors, ministers, traditional relationships and a greatly expanded party structure to offset Atiku’s regional appeal. That structure matters. The APC now enjoys an extraordinary advantage in the number of governors, lawmakers and local political networks under its control. Governors influence campaign financing, mobilisation and the organisation required to convert public sympathy into votes. The party’s challenge is that political machinery can mobilise supporters, but it cannot permanently insulate an incumbent from lived economic experience. The contest between structure and hardship The APC’s campaign argument will be that the most painful period of reform has passed. Inflation has moderated, foreign reserves have improved, economic growth has strengthened, and the Central Bank has begun adjusting interest rates. The administration will argue that removing the petrol subsidy and reforming the foreign-exchange market prevented a deeper fiscal crisis. The opposition’s reply is more immediate: food, transport, energy and business costs remain painfully high. That explains the political significance of the National Economic Council’s newly approved 90-day action plan. It prioritises food affordability, tax harmonisation, completion of high-impact projects, removal of investment bottlenecks and regulated household support. It also proposes a national dashboard to track projects and the use of savings from subsidy removal. On paper, these are reasonable interventions. The problem is timing. The presidential election is 86 days away, while the relief plan is designed to run for 90 days. Atiku’s campaign has therefore called it “election bait,” arguing that Nigerians are being asked to vote before the promised relief can be fully assessed. That is a partisan allegation, not proof that the programme is improper. But the calendar gives the criticism political force. The government can answer it only through early, measurable delivery. What food has become cheaper? Which households have received support? What projects have been completed? How much has been spent, by whom and under what criteria? Announcements will not be sufficient. The electorate needs receipts. The opposition’s unity problem While the APC prepares a major campaign launch, opposition parties are again discussing a consensus candidate. Representatives of the ADC, NDC, PRP, SDP, APM and PDP have inaugurated legal and media committees to develop a framework for cooperation. Atiku, Peter Obi, Donald Duke and Adewale Adebayo are among the names mentioned in the talks. Coalition organisers say negotiations are progressing towards a single candidate. That claim should be treated cautiously. The Independent National Electoral Commission has already published 18 presidential candidates, including Atiku for the ADC and Obi for the NDC. Agreeing that the opposition should unite is therefore much easier than determining who withdraws, who leads, what happens to the running mates and how supporters are transferred between parties. There is also no guarantee that voters will follow elite instructions. An Atiku endorsement of Obi would not automatically deliver Atiku’s northern vote. An Obi endorsement of Atiku would not automatically transfer younger urban voters or the South-East. Nigerian politicians often mistake negotiations among leaders for consolidation among electorates. The opposition nevertheless understands the arithmetic. Tinubu won in 2023 with 36.61 per cent of the valid votes; 8.79 million votes. Atiku and Obi together received more than 13 million. That does not mean a joint ticket would have automatically defeated Tinubu, because elections are shaped by turnout, geography and the constitutional requirement for national spread. But it shows why fragmentation remains the APC’s quiet ally. Unless the coalition produces a credible agreement quickly, it risks becoming a committee for managing defeat. The register question The emphasis on 103.43 million voters has also reopened an important transparency dispute. INEC says the total follows the addition of approximately 10.77 million new registrants. Atiku has demanded that the preliminary register be made available for public inspection, alleging that an online page intended for that purpose was empty. The allegation does not establish manipulation. Technical delays or publication problems are not evidence of a compromised register. But INEC should resolve the issue immediately. A national figure cannot substitute for a register that citizens and parties can scrutinise. The public must be able to identify duplicate entries, deceased persons, omissions and questionable registrations before the final roll is certified. If parties are already building campaign strategies around precise regional totals, voters deserve access to the underlying data. First, watch the language and attendance at Saturday’s Kaduna rally. A large gathering will demonstrate organisational capacity, but the more important question is whether influential northern leaders offer genuine commitments or merely perform ceremonial loyalty. Second, watch whether the 90-day economic plan produces identifiable benefits before election day. Its political credibility will depend on outcomes, not intentions. Third, watch the opposition negotiations. A consensus announced after ballots and campaign loyalties have hardened may be largely symbolic. Finally, watch INEC. Publication and scrutiny of the voter register will be an early test of whether the Commission intends to manage doubts proactively or react only after they become political crises. But the North’s 56 million registrations are not a blank cheque. Its voters are living with insecurity, expensive food, high transport costs and the uneven consequences of economic reform. The APC is campaigning on structure and patience. The opposition is campaigning on hardship and change, but without yet agreeing on whose change. item.description: Hundreds of protests were held in France Saturday as nationwide anger grows over the cost of living, with security forces massing to prevent a repeat of violence that marred demonstrations last week. Here are the latest developments: – ‘Calm’ in Paris – French police had arrested 135 people nationwide and seized a variety of weapons, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said, adding that, so far, “there has been no major incident”. Weapons confiscated included metal balls, lead pellets, fireworks, slingshots, steel balls, improvised weapons, a katana and airsoft weapons, he said. Paris police described the situation as “calm” at midday. – ‘Scandalous’ – Hundreds of demonstrators could be seen gathering at Porte d’Italie in Paris, where authorities have said they must begin the only authorised march. Union representative Murielle Guilbert told reporters it was “scandalous” that President Emmanuel Macron had forbidden protesters from demonstrating “where we wish to demonstrate”. “We are here today, quite obviously, because there is immense social anger in this country, and because wages have still not been increased to the level they should be,” she added. Paris police at the last minute ordered the union-organised march be moved from Bastille, in the centre, to the more remote Porte d’Italie on the southeastern rim. Unions said they reluctantly agreed. But the Yellow Vests — a loosely organised group that staged disruptive street protests against Macron eight years ago — indicated they would not comply. – Halloween protests called – One group organising Saturday’s demonstrations — the Yellow Vests — said they would hold another round of protests on October 31. Organisers called for rallies and a sit-in outside parliament and city halls nationwide, condemning the “authoritarian drift” of President Emmanuel Macron’s government and urging citizens to stand up for “public freedoms”. – Tear gas in Lyon – Police fired teargas to disperse some 150 people protesting in the southeastern city of Lyon, in an area banned to all demonstrations, an AFP journalist saw. Police fired several teargas grenades to clear the group near a university faculty and the city’s police station as part of nationwide rallies against the cost of living. The protest criticised both leading presidential candidate Le Pen and centrist Macron. “Macron resign. Le Pen in prison,” the crowd yelled. – Louvre, Orsay closed – The Louvre, d’Orsay, and Picasso museums, as well as the Grand Palais in Paris, were closed Saturday. The culture ministry had called on institutions to take every measure to ensure the safety of visitors and staff, and the protection of artworks. A country that ranks highly in one category may occupy a lower position in another, highlighting the different priorities and capabilities of armed forces worldwide. The top 10 countries with the largest active military forces are China, with 2,035,000 personnel; India, with 1,431,000; the United States, with 1,333,030; North Korea and Russia, with 1,320,000 each; Ukraine, with 900,000; Pakistan, with 660,000; Iran, with 610,000; Ethiopia, with 503,000; and Türkiye, with 481,000. The figures cover active personnel across the armed forces but exclude reservists and paramilitary organisations. North Korea’s high ranking reflects its emphasis on preparing for a potential conflict on the Korean Peninsula. Its military structure places considerable importance on ground forces, with significant strength positioned near the Demilitarised Zone separating the country from South Korea. Japan’s 2026 defence white paper also highlights the security challenges surrounding the Korean Peninsula and the military capabilities maintained by North Korea. Tank Ranks by Country China leads the ranking of countries with the largest tank inventories, followed by Russia, while North Korea occupies third place ahead of the United States. The figures illustrate the importance several countries continue to place on land-based military operations, although the number of tanks alone does not determine the effectiveness of an armoured force. Russia has 5,870 tanks, while China follows closely with 5,630. North Korea ranks third with 4,895 tanks, ahead of the United States, which has 4,666. India occupies fifth place with 3,913 tanks, followed by Egypt with 3,620. Pakistan ranks seventh with 2,677, while Iran is eighth with 2,675. Türkiye takes ninth place with 2,284 tanks, and Vietnam rounds out the top 10 with 1,999. North Korea’s extensive tank inventory reflects its long-standing focus on conventional ground warfare. Research published by the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI) indicates that the country operates a combination of older Soviet-inspired designs and newer equipment. Maintaining a large number of tanks can provide a military with substantial ground-firepower capacity. However, the age and technological sophistication of the vehicles also matter. Modern armour, targeting systems, sensors, weapons and battlefield communications can significantly affect the performance of tanks in combat. Consequently, a country with a larger inventory does not necessarily possess a more effective armoured force than one with fewer but more advanced vehicles. Military Aircraft The United States has the world’s largest military aircraft inventory, with 13,032 aircraft, placing it far ahead of other countries. Its fleet is more than three times the size of Russia’s and exceeds the combined totals of the next four countries in the ranking. Russia comes second with 4,237 military aircraft, followed by China with 3,529. India ranks fourth with 2,183, while South Korea occupies fifth place with 1,540. Pakistan follows with 1,429 aircraft, ahead of Japan, which has 1,397. Türkiye ranks eighth with 1,101, while Egypt has 1,088. France completes the top 10 with 974 military aircraft. The ranking includes aircraft across military branches, covering helicopters, transport planes, training aircraft and other military aviation assets, rather than combat jets alone. The United States’ substantial advantage reflects the requirements of maintaining military operations across multiple regions of the world. Its armed forces need to transport troops, equipment and supplies over long distances while supporting combat missions far from home bases. These operations depend on a broad aviation network that includes cargo aircraft, aerial refuelling tankers, helicopters and fighter jets. The ability to transport personnel and equipment and keep aircraft supplied with fuel is essential to sustaining military operations overseas. However, the difference between the United States and China becomes smaller when the comparison is restricted to fighter and interceptor aircraft. The United States has 1,791 fighters and interceptors, compared with China’s 1,443. This gives Washington an advantage of approximately 24 per cent in this category. The narrower gap demonstrates that the United States’ lead in total military aircraft is partly attributable to the size and diversity of its wider aviation fleet, rather than fighter aircraft alone. Naval Assets China has the world’s largest navy by the number of vessels in the Global Firepower ranking, with 841 naval assets. The United States follows with 465, while Russia ranks third with 343. The ranking reflects China’s expanding maritime capabilities and its extensive shipbuilding industry. Research by the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) has examined how China’s commercial shipbuilding infrastructure can also support military ship production, providing an industrial foundation for expanding its naval fleet. North Korea ranks fourth with 338 naval assets, followed by Sweden with 332. Indonesia occupies sixth place with 304 vessels, while Italy ranks seventh with 285. India is eighth with 279 naval assets, Thailand ranks ninth with 275, and Sri Lanka completes the top 10 with 275 vessels. China’s total of 841 vessels is substantially higher than the United States’ 465, but vessel counts provide only one measure of naval strength. The figures include different types of vessels, ranging from small patrol boats and coastal craft to larger warships. Each vessel contributes one unit to the total, regardless of its size, armament or operational role. As a result, a country with numerous smaller vessels may rank above another whose fleet contains fewer but significantly larger and more capable ships. The ranking changes when naval strength is measured by total fleet tonnage instead of vessel numbers. Under Global Firepower’s fleet-tonnage ranking, the United States takes first place, with approximately 2.6 times China’s total displacement. Fleet tonnage measures the combined displacement of a navy’s vessels and provides a different perspective on the scale of its maritime assets. Nevertheless, tonnage also has limitations. It does not independently measure a vessel’s weapons, technological sophistication, operational readiness or combat effectiveness. Taken together, the rankings demonstrate why military strength cannot be assessed through a single measure. Personnel numbers reveal the size of a country’s active force, tank inventories highlight its armoured capabilities, aircraft totals reflect its aviation resources, and naval counts offer insight into its maritime presence. However, equipment quality, training, logistics, technology and the ability to deploy forces effectively are also crucial to determining a military’s overall strength. item.title: Police Fire Tear Gas As New French Protests Kick Off
item.description: French police started firing tear gas at protesters Saturday as they stepped up security in major cities, aiming to prevent a repeat of rioting a week ago, on a day of fresh nationwide demonstrations over the high cost of living. Police in the southeast city of Lyon fired tear gas to disperse some 150 protesters near the city centre — where demonstrations had been banned — when they briefly tried to block a road, an AFP journalist saw. “The police are really mobile… They come and disperse marches before they even form,” said a 21-year-old student who had turned up to protest, speaking on condition of anonymity. Elsewhere, authorities and rattled shopkeepers geared up for potential new street violence. Protesters take part in a demonstration “against racism, fascism and imperialism” on the sidelines of the Congress of the Far-right party Rassemblement National (RN) in Orleans, central France on October 24, 2026. Near Paris’s Bastille neighbourhood, a clothing store had removed all its merchandise from shelves ahead of the demonstrations, while a nearby restaurant was boarded up with signs insisting it was “still open”. Many other retailers in the capital also had wooden boards covering their windows. The Louvre and the Musée d’Orsay museums were closed. The capital’s police said at midday officers had confiscated “various forbidden items” but described the situation as “calm”. In Marseille, riot squad vehicles, armoured trucks and a water cannon were parked in the city centre, while police elsewhere prepared for potential clashes. They were among 70,000 security personnel the interior ministry said were mobilised to counter the “high” threat of violence. item.content:encoded: French police started firing tear gas at protesters Saturday as they stepped up security in major cities, aiming to prevent a repeat of rioting a week ago, on a day of fresh nationwide demonstrations over the high cost of living. Police in the southeast city of Lyon fired tear gas to disperse some 150 protesters near the city centre — where demonstrations had been banned — when they briefly tried to block a road, an AFP journalist saw. “The police are really mobile… They come and disperse marches before they even form,” said a 21-year-old student who had turned up to protest, speaking on condition of anonymity. Elsewhere, authorities and rattled shopkeepers geared up for potential new street violence. Protesters take part in a demonstration “against racism, fascism and imperialism” on the sidelines of the Congress of the Far-right party Rassemblement National (RN) in Orleans, central France on October 24, 2026. Near Paris’s Bastille neighbourhood, a clothing store had removed all its merchandise from shelves ahead of the demonstrations, while a nearby restaurant was boarded up with signs insisting it was “still open”. Many other retailers in the capital also had wooden boards covering their windows. The Louvre and the Musée d’Orsay museums were closed. The capital’s police said at midday officers had confiscated “various forbidden items” but described the situation as “calm”. In Marseille, riot squad vehicles, armoured trucks and a water cannon were parked in the city centre, while police elsewhere prepared for potential clashes. They were among 70,000 security personnel the interior ministry said were mobilised to counter the “high” threat of violence. Protest Against Le Pen’s Party Adding to tensions, Marine Le Pen’s National Rally party held a congress in Orleans to launch her campaign for elections in six months to choose President Emmanuel Macron’s successor. Thousands of people yelling anti-fascist slogans marched on Saturday against Le Pen, and also against Macron, a pro-business centrist leader. “Macron resign. Le Pen in prison,” the crowd yelled. Police put their numbers at 11,000 while organisers said 26,000 took part. The unrest highlighted tensions in France ahead of the vote, which Le Pen is best-placed, according to surveys, to win. Last weekend saw rioters on the margins of the nationwide demonstrations clash with police, vandalise public buildings and loot hundreds of stores. Some 2,700 people were arrested, and the retail sector said shopowners were left with damage and stolen stock totalling hundreds of millions of euros. Macron attributed the worst of the violence to “ultra-left” groups that he said want to bring down the republic. Groups organising Saturday’s renewed demonstrations have accused Macron and his government of ignoring widespread public anger over rising costs, and over classroom conditions for students. Inflation in France, as elsewhere, has been sent surging by the Middle East war, started in February against Iran by US President Donald Trump and Israel. Protests have also been taking place in Italy, Belgium, Spain and Portugal over different issues, yet with some overlap on inflation and education problems. Italy has mobilised 500 troops to Milan after street violence there. Unions said they reluctantly would go along with that. But the Yellow Vests, who staged disruptive protests against Macron eight years ago, denounced an “authoritarian drift” and called for yet more demonstrations on October 31 for “the freedom to protest”. A shopworker in the city of Rennes told AFP: “Bans are sometimes worse. item.title: Which countries are best at maths? See top 10
item.description: China leads the world in mathematics performance among 15-year-old students, followed by Singapore and Macao, according to the latest Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) results published in September 2026. The ranking compares the average mathematics scores of students across participating countries and economies. item.title: FIFA: Infantino says backed by ‘vast majority’ in bid for re-election
item.description: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has said he has the backing of the “vast, vast majority” of member associations in his bid for re-election despite criticism of his aborted World Cup selloff plan. The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) rallied behind Infantino on Friday in a significant boost to the 56-year-old’s hopes of winning a fourth term in charge. Infantino’s future in the role was in doubt two months ago when he faced a furious backlash to his plan to sell off a portion of the commercial rights of competitions run by football’s world governing body to private investors. The heads of European football’s governing body UEFA, the AFC and CONCACAF, which runs the game in North and Central America, signed a letter saying football “belongs to no individual”. But Infantino, who apologised last week for the failed private investment project, is now in a strong position to secure re-election in March. “I think what is important is that in an organisation like FIFA, there can be different views, different points of view,” Infantino told the BBC on Saturday. “But if we are serious about democracy, about the democratic process, about believing that everyone has the same vote and the same voice all over the world, that football belongs to everyone, if we are serious about that, then we need to respect as well the views of the vast, vast majority. “I’m just coming back off Tokyo where the Asian Football Confederation has fully endorsed me. I was in Cape Verde where all African countries have endorsed me. I’m speaking to all associations everywhere in the world.” No other candidate has yet come forward to oppose Infantino with the deadline to do so less than a month away on November 18. He added: “There are different points of view it’s not always easy to bring them all under one roof but we need to respect and I do respect all opinions all views and then it will be up to the FIFA member associations to decide who they want as a president and how they want FIFA to be run.” The post FIFA: Infantino says backed by ‘vast majority’ in bid for re-election appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Alake’s attack on Atiku won’t cut food prices, ADC campaign fires back
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja The African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council has fired back at Information Minister Dele Alake over his allegations against former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, saying no amount of political propaganda can shield President Bola Tinubu’s administration from public anger over rising living costs. The council argued that Nigerians were more concerned about the cost of food, fuel and transportation than allegations of artificial intelligence manipulation and deepfakes, challenging Alake to produce evidence linking Atiku or the ADC to the alleged fabricated letter and video. In a statement on Saturday, Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, described Alake’s intervention as an attempt to divert attention from the government’s record, insisting that the economic hardship confronting Nigerians was real and undeniable. “Until then, his ‘fake news alert’ is an empty political stunt,” Shaibu said, challenging the minister to provide names, dates and forensic findings to substantiate his allegations. Citing petrol prices of about ₦1,400 per litre, diesel prices above ₦2,000 and food inflation hovering around 20 per cent, Shaibu said the economic pressures facing households could not be dismissed as fabricated information. item.title: 2027: Jigawa APC unveils campaign structure, names Namadi chairman
item.description: ‎ By Muhammad Inuwa ,Dutse ‎ The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Jigawa State has unveiled its campaign structure for the 2027 general elections, appointing Governor Umar Namadi as chairman and former governors Ali Sa’adu Birnin Kudu and Ibrahim Saminu Turaki as deputy chairmen. ‎ The structure is designed to coordinate campaign activities, strengthen party structures and mobilise grassroots support across the state’s 27 local government areas ahead of the elections. ‎ The appointments were announced in a statement dated October 22, 2026, and signed by the state APC chairman, Hon. Ahmed Garba. ‎ According to the statement, the party’s State Working Committee approved the composition of the campaign council following consultations with party leaders and stakeholders across the state. ‎ The council has six vice chairmen representing the three senatorial districts, with two representatives from each zone to ensure broad participation and effective coordination of campaign activities. ‎ For Jigawa North-East, Senator Muhammad Ibrahim and Senator Ibrahim Hassan Hadejia were appointed Vice Chairmen I and II, respectively. ‎ In Jigawa South-West, the Speaker of the Jigawa State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Haruna Aliyu Dangyatin, and Hon. Farouk Adamu Aliyu were named Vice Chairmen I and II. ‎ Similarly, Alhaji Jisa Gerawa and Hajiya Rabi Ishaq were appointed Vice Chairmen I and II for Jigawa North-West Senatorial District. ‎ The party also named Alhaji Lawan Yau Roni as director-general of the campaign council, responsible for coordinating its day-to-day activities and implementing campaign programmes. ‎ The council is expected to provide strategic direction, coordinate campaign operations and strengthen engagement with party leaders, members and supporters ahead of the 2027 general elections. ‎ Garba urged members of the council, party leaders and supporters to demonstrate unity, discipline, loyalty and commitment to the party’s electoral objectives. ‎ He reaffirmed the APC’s commitment to progressive governance, democratic development and advancing the interests of the people of Jigawa State, while calling on members to work together towards the party’s success in the forthcoming elections. Ahmed Garba. ‎ According to the statement, the party’s State Working Committee approved the composition of the campaign council following consultations with party leaders and stakeholders across the state. ‎ The council has six vice chairmen representing the three senatorial districts, with two representatives from each zone to ensure broad participation and effective coordination of campaign activities. ‎ For Jigawa North-East, Senator Muhammad Ibrahim and Senator Ibrahim Hassan Hadejia were appointed Vice Chairmen I and II, respectively. ‎ In Jigawa South-West, the Speaker of the Jigawa State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Haruna Aliyu Dangyatin, and Hon. Farouk Adamu Aliyu were named Vice Chairmen I and II. ‎ Similarly, Alhaji Jisa Gerawa and Hajiya Rabi Ishaq were appointed Vice Chairmen I and II for Jigawa North-West Senatorial District. ‎ The party also named Alhaji Lawan Yau Roni as director-general of the campaign council, responsible for coordinating its day-to-day activities and implementing campaign programmes. ‎ The council is expected to provide strategic direction, coordinate campaign operations and strengthen engagement with party leaders, members and supporters ahead of the 2027 general elections. ‎ Garba urged members of the council, party leaders and supporters to demonstrate unity, discipline, loyalty and commitment to the party’s electoral objectives. ‎ He reaffirmed the APC’s commitment to progressive governance, democratic development and advancing the interests of the people of Jigawa State, while calling on members to work together towards the party’s success in the forthcoming elections. item.title: Jigawa govt denies giving houses to Kannywood actors
item.description: ‎ ‎By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse ‎ ‎Jigawa State Government has dismissed allegations that it allocated houses in the Danmodi Housing Estate in Ringim to popular APC musician Dauda Kahutu Rarara and members of the Triple R group. ‎ ‎Dady Ringim, a new media aide to Governor Umar Namadi, described the allegation as false and lacking factual basis while reacting to the controversy on social media. ‎ ‎The controversy followed a viral video in which Rarara and members of Triple R allegedly claimed that the governor had allocated houses to them”. The video has triggered reactions from opposition figures and other social media users in the state. ‎Among those who criticised the alleged allocation was Zakari Kafin Hausa, a former aide to Governor Namadi and a prominent critic of his administration and ADC Candidate for Auyo/Kafin Hausa House of Representatives in the 2027 election. ‎ ‎In his Facebook post, Kafin Hausa questioned the reported allocation of the houses, particularly as the housing project was allegedly financed with public funds. ‎ ‎ “There are certain decisions taken by this administration that I am wondering whether it is the Umar Namadi we have always known making them or he has been replaced with ‘Jibrin from Sudan.’” ‎ ‎He also questioned why public housing projects should be allocated in such a manner. ‎ ‎However, reacting to the criticism, Ringim accused Kafin Hausa of overlooking the governor’s achievements, arguing that Namadi’s projects and policies were strengthening his popularity and re-election prospects. According to him, “The Triple R statement does not mean the Governor has gift them Houses, they are trying to establish the fact that the Governor has constructed the affordable Housing Estate for the People of the state. “The Danmodi Housing Estate was constructed across the whole 27 Local Government of the state and are available for the citizens whoever meet the requirements” he said. “What they are doing are doing it to advertise the good work of Governor Umar Namadi, not only Housing Estate including Tsangaya, Roads, Health, Agriculture among other.” ‎He said the governor’s achievements were making a lasting impression on the people, adding that “politics is not built on rhetoric alone; it requires action and the trust of the people.” ‎ ‎Ringim expressed confidence that voters would determine the state’s political future, insisting that the administration’s performance was helping to build a lasting legacy, particularly among young people. ‎ ‎He urged political actors to verify information before making public allegations, warning that political differences should not be allowed to encourage the spread of misinformation. ‎ ‎The controversy has generated debate on social media over the alleged allocation of the houses and the management of publicly funded housing projects in Jigawa State. item.title: 10 killed as armed bandits raid Taraba community, loot food stores
item.description: By Femi Bolaji, Jalingo No fewer than ten residents were reportedly gunned down on Friday afternoon when a large gang of heavily armed bandits invaded Binnari village in Taraba State, unleashing intense gunfire and looting food supplies from shops. According to a police statement issued by the Taraba State Police Command Public Relations Officer, ASP Victor Mshelizah, the tragic attack occurred on Friday, October 23, 2026, at about 3:00 p.m., shortly after residents concluded Jumu’ah prayers. The assailants, numbering in their dozens, threw the rural community into pandemonium as they shot indiscriminately before pillaging food items and provision stores. Operatives attached to the Binnari police station, upon receiving distress calls, mobilised to the scene alongside community volunteers, recovering ten corpses bearing fatal gunshot wounds. The victims have since been handed over to their respective families and buried in accordance with Islamic rites. Reacting to the carnage, the State Commissioner of Police, CP Edwin Ogbeghagha, placed security formations across the area on red alert and ordered the immediate deployment of joint tactical teams comprising the Nigeria Police Force, Police Mobile Force (PMF), and the Nigerian Army to comb the surrounding terrain. The command urged residents of Binnari and neighbouring settlements to remain calm, avoid panic peddling, and cooperate with security operatives by sharing actionable intelligence that will lead to the apprehension of the fleeing attackers. item.title: 360 Woman Africa Annual Conference Brings Leaders in Business and Technology Together to Shape Women’s Future in the new Age of Artificial Intelligence (AI)
item.description: The social enterprise holds its 8th annual conference, THE SHIFT, on 31 October, 2026 at Glitz Event Center, Oniru, Lekki, Lagos 360 Woman Africa is a non-profit organization that champions skills development for women in business and leadership. This year, it marks 10 years of bold, transformative impact and hosts its 8th annual conference. The conference convenes some of Nigeria’s most influential voices in banking, commerce, technology, and beauty- leaders who have built institutions and shaped industries- to help women navigate one of the defining shifts of our time: the rise of artificial intelligence. Mrs. Ibukun Awosika, former Chairman of First Bank of Nigeria, will deliver the keynote. She will be joined by: Mrs. Tara Fela-Durotoye, founder, House of Tara International Prince Nnamdi Ekeh, CEO, Konga Group; Dr. Olubayo Adekanmbi, founder, Data Science Nigeria, Dr. Yvonne Chioma Ofodile, MD/CEO Zetile Oil and Gas Ltd, Zetile Stores Ltd and Founder, 360 Woman Africa amongst other leading global experts The theme of the conference is THE SHIFT: Designing Women’s Relevance in an AI-Intelligent World. Through panel sessions and hands-on AI skills workshops, the speakers will share practical insights on how women can lead, build, and stay relevant in their careers, businesses, and lives as AI reshapes the economy. Dr. Yvonne Chioma Ofodile, founder of 360 Woman Africa and convener of the 360 Woman Africa Annual Conference , said: “AI is changing how careers, businesses and life work. Women who quickly embrace, adapt, and learn to use it will 10x their businesses, homes, and careers. Those who do not may be left behind. This conference will show women how to use AI to build, scale and stay relevant in a fast-paced society.” More than 1,500 women founders, executives and professionals are expected to attend. Beyond the conference, 360 Woman Africa’s enterprise development platform for women-led businesses continues to lead boldly through its grant program, which has given out over ₦30 million to date. Registration is open at www.360womanafrica.com . About 360 Woman Africa Founded in [2016] by Dr. Yvonne Chioma Ofodile, 360 Woman Africa is a leadership and enterprise development organisation equipping African women to lead, build and thrive in a modern economy. Its work spans the Annual Conference, enterprise training programmes including its Mini-MBA, and the 360 Woman Africa Enterprise Fund, which provides equity-free grants to women-led businesses. About Dr. Yvonne Chioma Ofodile Dr. Yvonne Chioma Ofodile is the Founder and Convener of 360 Woman Africa and Chief Executive Officer of Zetile Group. A UK-certified coach, she has spent over a decade building platforms that connect women entrepreneurs to skills, networks and capital. item.title: Kaduna Presidential Rally: Atiku is butterfly thinking itself a bird – Keyamo
item.description: Festus Keyamo, Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, has described Atiku Abubakar as a butterfly that thinks it is a bird, given his “blistering online attack against the APC (All Progressives Congress), particularly in the North”. The APC is scheduled to flag off its presidential campaign in Kaduna on Saturday. According to Keyamo, Atiku Abubakar, the presidential candidate of African Democratic Congress, ADC, was banking on the bulk of Northern votes to see him through in 2027, knowing that he has no inroads at all into the South. Therefore, Keyamo said in a statement, Atiku has taken to the “common but cheap tactic” of positioning cameras then get people to tear down the posters of President Bola Tinubu, and then post the videos online. “The other tactic is to disseminate disinformation claiming that any support the President is seen to receive in the North is procured only through the massive deployment of financial resources. “Hence the fake letter alleging a N2.3 trillion deployment for the Kaduna rally. The intention is to generate a hoopla that will create a groundswell of public opinion that President Tinubu has been ‘massively rejected’ in the North.” Keyamo said given the mood of the country, the South deserves to complete eight years in the presidency. Also, he added, in 2023, Atiku lost across the Middle Belt, all southern states, except Osun State. Projecting on 2027 votes, Keyamo said with the APC structures in the North backing Tinubu, Atiku Abubakar has seen that his demographic calculation for the 2027 elections regarding northern votes is evaporating. Therefore, he noted, Atiku resorted to desperate tactics. “He knows that even if he wins in some parts of the North and the President comes a close second, the election is as good as over, because those differences would be wiped out by his heavy defeat in the Middle Belt and the South. “Atiku Abubakar thinks he is the Buhari of 2015, who swept the Northern votes. He thinks that was a display of ethnic support. He fails to realise that his past puts him poles apart from a Muhammadu Buhari,” Keyamo said. item.description: By Anayo Okoli A birthday celebration organised by a famous Enugu socialite, Nnaji Izuchukwu, popularly known as Stone, at a hotel in the Asata area of Enugu turned fatal, leading to his death. The celebrant, Izuchukwu Nnaji, allegedly died from gunshot injuries he sustained during the ensuing police operation. The exact circumstances surrounding the shooting remained unclear. item.title: Chelsea vs Tottenham: Preview, team news, possible line-ups
item.description: Chelsea will look to extend their winning run in the Premier League when they host Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge on Saturday in a London derby that could have significant implications for both sides. Chelsea have won four, drawn one and lost two of their opening seven league matches, leaving them in the top four. Their recent results have also boosted confidence, with a 5-1 victory over Bournemouth followed by a 2-0 win away to Everton last weekend. Pedro Neto scored twice against Everton as Chelsea ended a run of 22 Premier League matches without a clean sheet. The Blues will now attempt to record three consecutive league victories for the first time since February. The West London club have won their last six league meetings with Tottenham. Another victory on Saturday would set a new club record for consecutive league wins against their London rivals. Tottenham, meanwhile, ended a six-game winless start to the league campaign with a 3-1 victory over Coventry. James Maddison, Omar Marmoush and Ben Davies scored to give Roberto De Zerbi’s side a much-needed result. The win was Tottenham’s fourth Premier League victory in 2026 and the first time in 36 top-flight matches that they had scored more than twice. Despite the result, Spurs remain 16th in the table, although they are only three points behind the top nine. They will need to improve their away record against Chelsea to secure another positive result. Tottenham have won only once in their last 34 Premier League visits to Stamford Bridge, recording 11 draws and 24 defeats. Their most recent victory there came in the 2017-18 season, when Mauricio Pochettino guided them to a 3-1 win. Spurs have also lost their last six London derbies in the league and will be keen to avoid extending that run. Team news Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez is set to miss the match after undergoing surgery for a fractured jaw sustained during the win over Everton. He joins Reece James, Jamie Gittens, Pep Chavarria and Emmanuel Emegha on the injury list. Malo Gusto, however, is available again after recovering from illness. Mike Penders is expected to start in goal in Martinez’s absence. The 21-year-old could become Chelsea’s youngest goalkeeper to start a Premier League match. For Tottenham, Rodrigo Bentancur remains suspended and will serve the second match of his three-game ban. Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert, Lucas Bergvall and Destiny Udogie are also sidelined with knee injuries, while Savio is unavailable because of a muscle problem. Mykhaylo Mudryk, who is on loan from Chelsea, is ineligible to face his parent club and is also recovering from an ankle injury. Tosin Adarabioyo is a doubt with a calf problem, but Pedro Porro, Omar Marmoush and Andrew Robertson have been passed fit to play. Possible line-ups Chelsea: Penders; Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill; Neto, Caicedo, Henderson, Hato; Palmer, Rogers; Pedro. item.title: Campaign Turns Ugly As Israeli Election Nears
item.description: Days ahead of close-fought Israeli elections, campaigns have gone into overdrive with poor-taste jibes and inflammatory attacks against candidates, sometimes crossing red lines. Fuelled in part by a boom in AI-generated images flooding social media, candidates and activists are seeking to portray their opponents as weak, untrustworthy or damaging for the country as they play on stereotypes and fears to sway public opinion. The electioneering has at times turned personal, with some candidates who lost loved ones in the wars following Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack even having their bereavement dragged into the campaign. Ahead of Tuesday’s vote, polls show Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc neck and neck with that of his main centre-right rival Gadi Eisenkot. On Wednesday, Eisenkot posted a video on X wishing Netanyahu a happy 77th birthday that featured a slate of AI-generated characters including a Hamas member speaking from a tunnel. “What can we wish for the person who has been protecting us for 20 years?” the militant says, evoking theories that the premier has deliberately helped the Islamist movement stay in power in Gaza, charges vehemently denied by Netanyahu. Soon after, an AI depiction of Iran’s supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei pops up, telling Netanyahu: “One more round without victory and I’ll make you a bomb as a present.” Netanyahu has also liberally weaponised AI-generated content against his rival. In July, he posted a video depicting Eisenkot rejecting a hug from a young man wearing a T-shirt with the slogan “Israel unity” and instead embracing Arab-Israeli candidate Mansour Abbas. item.title: Edo Govt, NLC Resolve Dispute As NUEE Moves To Restore Electricity
item.description: Electricity supply is set to be restored in Edo State after Governor Monday Okpebholo and leaders of organised labour settled the dispute over recognition of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) caretaker committee in the state. According to a Press Release by the Chief Press Secretary to the governor, Patrick Ebojele, the agreement was reached at a closed-door meeting in Abuja convened by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume. Also present were NLC President, Comrade Joe Ajaero; Minister of Labour and Employment, Dr Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi; and former Edo State Governor and ex-NLC President, Senator Adams Oshiomhole. Speaking to journalists after the meeting, Governor Okpebholo said the parties had resolved the matter. According to him, the state government would recognise the caretaker committee and work with labour leaders on arrangements for a substantive election. “There is no issue actually, and we have resolved the issues that border the NLC caretaker committee in Edo,” he said. The Governor of Edo State, Monday Okpebholo, the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume, NLC President, Comrade Joe Ajaero, Minister of Labour and Employment, Dr Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi, former Edo State Governor and ex-NLC President, Senator Adams Oshiomhole and others at the settlement meeting in Abuja. Ajaero confirmed the agreement and thanked the Governor, Akume, Dingyadi and Oshiomhole for their roles. He said labour had agreed to work with the state government on recognising the caretaker committee, organising a substantive election, and addressing the rights and privileges due to the committee. “Consequently, power will be restored in Edo,” Ajaero said. Oshiomhole described the dispute as a communication gap, which he said had now been resolved. He said the reason for continuing the action no longer existed. He also noted the Governor’s offer to rebuild trust between the Edo State Government and organised labour, and said renewed cooperation was needed to maintain industrial harmony. Dingyadi said the parties had agreed to work together for the peace and progress of Edo State and Nigeria. He said the NLC would conduct a substantive election in Edo within three to six months. “The principal issue, which is electricity, is going to be restored immediately,” the minister said. Akume commended the participants for their willingness to settle the matter through dialogue. The power outage followed two related but separate disputes. The first was an industrial disagreement between BEDC Electricity Plc and the National Union of Electricity Employees (NUEE) over workers’ pay and welfare. The second was a leadership dispute with the Edo State NLC, led by Joseph Igbafe, over recognition of its caretaker committee.
